title: ChaseAI: client document collection and checking for small accounting firms
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: Collects clients' tax and bookkeeping documents by email or WhatsApp, with no portal password, and checks with AI that each file is the right one for the right period.
hook: "I send three reminders, the client finally uploads something, and it's last year's bank statement."
story:
**Emma runs a 4-person bookkeeping firm in Manchester with 120 clients.** Every tax season she sends checklists by email. Clients forget their portal passwords, send blurry photos, or upload the wrong year. On average clients take **5 days** to send what she asks for, and many need several reminders.

In peak season her team spends hours a week just asking for and checking documents. A missing page is often found only when the return is half done. With ChaseAI, each client gets a **magic link or replies by email or WhatsApp**, and the AI immediately says "this is the 2024 statement, we need 2025" before Emma even opens the file.
whyNow: Document collection became the number-one workflow challenge for accounting firms in 2025, named by 55% of about 816 firm owners. Firms are ready for AI: 98% of accounting firms now use AI, most of them daily.
evidence: 55% of about 816 accounting firm owners named document collection their biggest workflow challenge in 2025 (secondary coverage) [CPA Practice Advisor]

whyReal.title: It is the top complaint
whyReal.text: Two separate 2025 surveys (CPA Practice Advisor, Mango) rank document collection as the biggest workflow or client-communication problem.

whyReal.title: Tools chase but do not check
whyReal.text: Most tools send reminders but nobody checks what arrives: wrong year, missing pages, wrong account. Practitioners say vague requests fail and clients forget portal passwords (SmartVault).

whyReal.title: Firms already pay for software
whyReal.text: Content Snare ($29–99/month), TaxDome (from $695/year), Financial Cents ($19/user/month) and Dext ($31.50/user/month) prove the willingness to pay.

whyReal.title: Same engine as SubDocs
whyReal.text: If construction firms are slow to buy, the same document code can be re-skinned for accountants in days.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: Accounting and bookkeeping firms with 1–15 people.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK, Ireland, the Nordics and the EU; later US tax preparers.

solution.title: Import clients and checklists
solution.text: the firm uploads its client list and picks a checklist template (UK Self Assessment, Swedish K10/INK1, Irish Form 11).

solution.title: No-login collection
solution.text: each client gets a magic-link upload page and their own inbound email address; WhatsApp in version 1.1.

solution.title: AI checks every file
solution.text: the LLM classifies each upload and validates document type, period and name match.

solution.title: Missing / incorrect list
solution.text: the client sees exactly what is still missing or wrong, in plain words.

solution.title: Escalating reminders
solution.text: email first, then WhatsApp, until the checklist is complete.

solution.title: Export and digest
solution.text: files go to Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive; the firm gets a weekly status digest.

must: Firm dashboard and client list (CSV import)
Magic-link upload page and inbound email address per client
LLM classification and validation of uploads (type, period, name match)
Export to Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive + weekly digest

techStack: OCR + small LLM for classification and validation

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Jonatan contacts 100 UK and Swedish bookkeepers: "send us your client list and checklist; we will chase your clients and tell you what is missing, free for 2 weeks". Run it by hand with a shared inbox, Google Forms upload and ChatGPT to check files. Success = 3+ firms using it and at least one agreeing to pay €29+.
Victor reuses the document engine: client list, checklists, magic links, inbound email, AI validation.
Reminders, exports, weekly digest, Stripe billing; move pilot firms onto the product.
Add WhatsApp; push before the next tax deadline, when the pain peaks.

risks.risk: Crowded market; Karbon or TaxDome can add AI checks
risks.answer: Win on the narrow wedge: validation of each upload, no-login replies and UK/Nordic/Irish checklists.

risks.risk: Financial documents bring GDPR and security duties
risks.answer: EU hosting, encryption and a data processing agreement; Victor's security skills are a selling point.

risks.risk: Demand is seasonal around tax deadlines
risks.answer: Sell bookkeeping (monthly) as well as year-end; time outreach before deadlines.

questions: Walk me through the last client whose documents arrived late: what happened, and how many reminders did it take?
How many hours per week do you or your staff spend asking for or checking documents in peak season?
What do you use today (portal, email, Content Snare, TaxDome), and what do clients hate about it?
How often do clients send the wrong or an incomplete document, and how do you notice?
If a tool cut chasing time in half, what would you pay per month, and who decides?
